newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk party urges Ciller prosecution in scandal.
newsitem.headline: Turk party urges Ciller prosecution in scandal.

text.p: Around 80 members of a left-wing party on Monday petitioned prosecutors to charge Turkey's deputy prime minister, Tansu Ciller, with links to far-right gangsters at the centre of a security scandal.

The Freedom and Solidarity Party members presented separate identical petitions to the Ankara prosecutors office calling for a trial against Ciller, a former interior minister and a government MP for allegedly forming an armed gang.
The three have been linked by the media to claims that Turkey used right-wing criminals for political killings in exchange for turning a blind eye to their drug-trafficking activities.
"A historical opportunity to expose unsolved murders and the drugs and arms smuggling that have been going on in our country for years...has presented itself," the petition said.

Party officials said they were not hopeful charges would be pressed. The three enjoy parliamentary immunity but under Turkish law the prosecutor must at least make a preliminary investigation and reply to the requests.

Another prosecutor is investigating a traffic accident in the western town of Susurluk last month that brought the scandal to light. The MP, who also heads a pro-state Kurdish militia, a wanted gangster and a senior policemen were travelling in the same car when it crashed.
